akhfash:3-3.t: His words ﴿مِن شَرِّ غَاسِقٍ إِذَا وَقَبَ﴾: you say "غَسَقَ" "يَغْسِقُ" "غُسُوقاً", and it is "darkness" (الظلمة). And "وَقَب" "يَقِبُ" "وُقُوباً", which is entering into a thing.

daas-irab:1-1.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿أَعُوذُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿بِرَبِّ﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿الْفَلَقِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).

daas-irab:2-2.t: ﴿مِنْ شَرِّ﴾ the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) أعوذ. ﴿ما﴾ a relative noun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿خَلَقَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause).

daas-irab:3-3.t: ﴿وَمِنْ شَرِّ﴾ the two are conjoined (maʿṭūfān) to what precedes them. ﴿غاسِقٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿إِذا﴾ an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān). ﴿وَقَبَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa).

daas-irab:4-4.t: ﴿وَمِنْ شَرِّ النَّفَّاثاتِ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿فِي الْعُقَدِ﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) what precedes them.

daas-irab:5-5.t: ﴿وَمِنْ شَرِّ حاسِدٍ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿إِذا﴾ an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān). ﴿حَسَدَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa).

farraa:1-1.t:
[151/b] His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ ٱلْفَلَقِ﴾.
«الفلق» is the dawn; one says: it is clearer than the break (فلق) of dawn, and the parting (فرق) of dawn. The Prophet ﷺ had fallen gravely ill, and one day, as he was between sleep and waking, two angels came to him. One of them said: What is his ailment? The other said: He has a spell (طبّ) [placed] in a well, under a rock in it. The Prophet ﷺ woke up and sent ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir with a group of men to the well, and he brought out the sorcery. It was a bowstring with eleven knots in it; and whenever they untied a knot, he found relief, until the knots were untied, and it was as if he had been released from a tether. He was commanded to seek refuge with these two surahs, which are eleven verses, the number of the knots. The one who bewitched him was Labīd ibn Aʿṣam.

farraa:3-3.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمِن شَرِّ غَاسِقٍ إِذَا وَقَبَ﴾.
«الغاسق» is the night. "إذا وقب": when it enters into everything and grows dark. One says: غسق and أغسق.

farraa:4-4.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمِن شَرِّ ٱلنَّفَّاثَاتِ فِي ٱلْعُقَدِ﴾.
They are the sorceresses who blow their sorcery. «ومِنْ شَرِّ حاسدٍ إِذَا حَسَدَ»: meaning Labīd, who bewitched him.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Falaq
Meccan
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُلْ أعُوذُ بِرَبِّ الفَلَقِ﴾ ("Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of the daybreak"): it is the falaq of the morning, i.e. its light; one also says ”فَرَقُ الصُّبْحِ“, and one says ”هُوَ أبْيَنُ مِن فَلَقِ الصُّبْحِ“ ("it is clearer than the break of morning"). And the meaning of ”اَلْفَلْقُ“ is creation. Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿فالِقُ الإصْباحِ﴾ [al-Anʿām: 96] ("the Cleaver of daybreak") and ﴿فالِقُ الحَبِّ والنَّوى﴾ [al-Anʿām: 95] ("the Cleaver of grain and date-stone"). Likewise He cleaves the earth with vegetation and the clouds with rain. If you reflect on creation, it becomes clear to you that most of His creating is through cleaving open; so al-falaq is all created things, and the break of morning is part of that.

zajjaj:3-3.t: ﴿وَمِن شَرِّ غاسِقٍ إذا وقَبَ﴾ ("and from the evil of darkness when it settles"): by ”غاسِقٍ“ the night is meant. ﴿إذا وقَبَ﴾: when it enters. The night was called ”غاسِقٌ“ — and Allah knows best — because it is colder than the day, and ”اَلْغاسِقُ“ is the cold.

zajjaj:4-4.t: ﴿وَمِن شَرِّ النَّفّاثاتِ في العُقَدِ﴾ ("and from the evil of the blowers on knots"): ”اَلنَّفّاثاتُ“ are the sorceresses; they blow (tanfuthu), i.e. they spit without saliva, as if it were blowing, as everyone who performs incantations does.
